title: She Walks in Beauty
author: Lord Byron
lines: She walks in beauty, like the night
Of cloudless climes and starry skies;
And all that's best of dark and bright
Meet in her aspect and her eyes;
Thus mellowed to that tender light
Which heaven to gaudy day denies.

title: Sonnet 18
author: William Shakespeare
lines: Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
Thou art more lovely and more temperate:
Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May,
And summer's lease hath all too short a date.

title: How Do I Love Thee (Sonnet 43)
author: Elizabeth Barrett Browning
lines: How do I love thee? Let me count the ways.
I love thee to the depth and breadth and height
My soul can reach, when feeling out of sight
For the ends of being and ideal grace.

title: A Red, Red Rose
author: Robert Burns
lines: O my Luve is like a red, red rose
That's newly sprung in June;
O my Luve is like the melody
That's sweetly played in tune.

title: Bright Star
author: John Keats
lines: Bright star, would I were stedfast as thou art—
Not in lone splendour hung aloft the night
And watching, with eternal lids apart,
Like nature's patient, sleepless Eremite.

title: Love's Philosophy
author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
lines: The fountains mingle with the river
And the rivers with the ocean,
The winds of heaven mix for ever
With a sweet emotion;
Nothing in the world is single;
All things by a law divine
In one spirit meet and mingle.
Why not I with thine?

title: The Good-Morrow
author: John Donne
lines: And now good-morrow to our waking souls,
Which watch not one another out of fear;
For love, all love of other sights controls,
And makes one little room an everywhere.

title: To Be One with Each Other
author: George Eliot
lines: What greater thing is there for two human souls
than to feel that they are joined for life—
to strengthen each other in all labour,
to rest on each other in all sorrow.

title: Meeting at Night
author: Robert Browning
lines: Then a mile of warm sea-scented beach;
Three fields to cross till a farm appears;
A tap at the pane, the quick sharp scratch
And blue spurt of a lighted match,
And a voice less loud, through its joys and fears,
Than the two hearts beating each to each!

title: Wild Nights – Wild Nights!
author: Emily Dickinson
lines: Wild nights - Wild nights!
Were I with thee
Wild nights should be
Our luxury!

title: Annabel Lee
author: Edgar Allan Poe
lines: But we loved with a love that was more than love—
I and my Annabel Lee—
With a love that the wingèd seraphs of Heaven
Coveted her and me.

title: The Sun Rising
author: John Donne
lines: She's all states, and all princes I,
Nothing else is.
Princes do but play us; compared to this,
All honour's mimic, all wealth alchemy.

title: Sonnet 116
author: William Shakespeare
lines: Let me not to the marriage of true minds
Admit impediments. Love is not love
Which alters when it alteration finds,
Or bends with the remover to remove.

title: When You Are Old
author: W. B. Yeats
lines: When you are old and grey and full of sleep,
And nodding by the fire, take down this book,
And slowly read, and dream of the soft look
Your eyes had once, and of their shadows deep.

title: She Was a Phantom of Delight
author: William Wordsworth
lines: She was a Phantom of delight
When first she gleamed upon my sight;
A lovely Apparition, sent
To be a moment's ornament.

title: To My Dear and Loving Husband
author: Anne Bradstreet
lines: If ever two were one, then surely we.
If ever man were loved by wife, then thee;
If ever wife was happy in a man,
Compare with me, ye women, if you can.

title: Give All to Love
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: Give all to love;
Obey thy heart;
Friends, kindred, days,
Estate, good-fame,
Plans, credit and the Muse,—
Nothing refuse.

title: My True Love Hath My Heart
author: Sir Philip Sidney
lines: My true love hath my heart, and I have his,
By just exchange one for the other given:
I hold his dear, and mine he cannot miss;
There never was a better bargain driven.

title: Music, When Soft Voices Die
author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
lines: Music, when soft voices die,
Vibrates in the memory—
Odours, when sweet violets sicken,
Live within the sense they quicken.

title: First Love
author: John Clare
lines: I ne'er was struck before that hour
With love so sudden and so sweet,
Her face it bloomed like a sweet flower
And stole my heart away complete.

title: Love and Friendship
author: Emily Brontë
lines: Love is like the wild rose-briar,
Friendship like the holly-tree—
The holly is dark when the rose-briar blooms
But which will bloom most constantly?

title: The Passionate Shepherd to His Love
author: Christopher Marlowe
lines: Come live with me and be my love,
And we will all the pleasures prove,
That valleys, groves, hills, and fields,
Woods, or steepy mountain yields.

title: Longing
author: Matthew Arnold
lines: Come to me in my dreams, and then
By day I shall be well again!
For so the night will more than pay
The hopeless longing of the day.

title: A Birthday
author: Christina Rossetti
lines: My heart is like a singing bird
Whose nest is in a watered shoot;
My heart is like an apple-tree
Whose boughs are bent with thickset fruit.

title: The Road Not Taken
author: Robert Frost
lines: Two roads diverged in a yellow wood,
And sorry I could not travel both
And be one traveler, long I stood
And looked down one as far as I could
To where it bent in the undergrowth.

title: Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening
author: Robert Frost
lines: The woods are lovely, dark and deep,
But I have promises to keep,
And miles to go before I sleep,
And miles to go before I sleep.

title: Invictus
author: William Ernest Henley
lines: It matters not how strait the gate,
How charged with punishments the scroll,
I am the master of my fate,
I am the captain of my soul.

title: If—
author: Rudyard Kipling
lines: If you can keep your head when all about you
Are losing theirs and blaming it on you,
If you can trust yourself when all men doubt you,
But make allowance for their doubting too;

title: "Hope" is the thing with feathers
author: Emily Dickinson
lines: "Hope" is the thing with feathers -
That perches in the soul -
And sings the tune without the words -
And never stops - at all -

title: Leisure
author: W. H. Davies
lines: What is this life if, full of care,
We have no time to stand and stare.
No time to stand beneath the boughs
And stare as long as sheep or cows.

title: Ozymandias
author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
lines: And on the pedestal these words appear:
'My name is Ozymandias, King of Kings;
Look on my Works, ye Mighty, and despair!'
Nothing beside remains. Round the decay
Of that colossal Wreck, boundless and bare
The lone and level sands stretch far away.

title: The Lake Isle of Innisfree
author: W. B. Yeats
lines: I will arise and go now, and go to Innisfree,
And a small cabin build there, of clay and wattles made;
Nine bean-rows will I have there, a hive for the honey-bee,
And live alone in the bee-loud glade.

title: I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud
author: William Wordsworth
lines: I wandered lonely as a cloud
That floats on high o'er vales and hills,
When all at once I saw a crowd,
A host, of golden daffodils;
Beside the lake, beneath the trees,
Fluttering and dancing in the breeze.

title: Sea Fever
author: John Masefield
lines: I must go down to the seas again, to the lonely sea and the sky,
And all I ask is a tall ship and a star to steer her by;
And the wheel's kick and the wind's song and the white sail's shaking,
And a grey mist on the sea's face, and a grey dawn breaking.

title: The Tyger
author: William Blake
lines: Tyger Tyger, burning bright,
In the forests of the night;
What immortal hand or eye,
Could frame thy fearful symmetry?

title: Pied Beauty
author: Gerard Manley Hopkins
lines: Glory be to God for dappled things –
For skies of couple-colour as a brinded cow;
For rose-moles all in stipple upon trout that swim;
Fresh-firecoal chestnut-falls; finches' wings.

title: Loveliest of Trees
author: A. E. Housman
lines: Loveliest of trees, the cherry now
Is hung with bloom along the bough,
And stands about the woodland ride
Wearing white for Eastertide.

title: Crossing the Bar
author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
lines: Sunset and evening star,
And one clear call for me!
And may there be no moaning of the bar,
When I put out to sea.

title: Fog
author: Carl Sandburg
lines: The fog comes
on little cat feet.
It sits looking
over harbor and city
on silent haunches
and then moves on.

title: Sonnet 130
author: William Shakespeare
lines: My mistress' eyes are nothing like the sun;
Coral is far more red than her lips' red;
If snow be white, why then her breasts are dun;
If hairs be wires, black wires grow on her head.

title: So We'll Go No More a Roving
author: Lord Byron
lines: So, we'll go no more a roving
So late into the night,
Though the heart be still as loving,
And the moon be still as bright.

title: I Am Not Yours
author: Sara Teasdale
lines: I am not yours, not lost in you,
Not lost, although I long to be
Lost as a candle lit at noon,
Lost as a snowflake in the sea.

title: Remember
author: Christina Rossetti
lines: Remember me when I am gone away,
Gone far away into the silent land;
When you can no more hold me by the hand,
Nor I half turn to go yet turning stay.

title: She Dwelt Among the Untrodden Ways
author: William Wordsworth
lines: She dwelt among the untrodden ways
Beside the springs of Dove,
A Maid whom there were none to praise
And very few to love:

title: Now Sleeps the Crimson Petal
author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
lines: Now sleeps the crimson petal, now the white;
Nor waves the cypress in the palace walk;
Now lies the Earth all Danaë to the stars,
And all thy heart lies open unto me.

title: A Valediction: Forbidding Mourning
author: John Donne
lines: Our two souls therefore, which are one,
Though I must go, endure not yet
A breach, but an expansion,
Like gold to airy thinness beat.

title: Nothing Gold Can Stay
author: Robert Frost
lines: Nature's first green is gold,
Her hardest hue to hold.
Her early leaf's a flower;
But only so an hour.

title: Believe Me, if All Those Endearing Young Charms
author: Thomas Moore
lines: Believe me, if all those endearing young charms,
Which I gaze on so fondly to-day,
Were to change by to-morrow, and fleet in my arms,
Like fairy-gifts fading away,

title: My Heart's in the Highlands
author: Robert Burns
lines: My heart's in the Highlands, my heart is not here,
My heart's in the Highlands a-chasing the deer;
A-chasing the wild-deer, and following the roe,
My heart's in the Highlands, wherever I go.

title: Love's Secret
author: William Blake
lines: Never seek to tell thy love,
Love that never told can be;
For the gentle wind does move
Silently, invisibly.

title: A Dream Within a Dream
author: Edgar Allan Poe
lines: Take this kiss upon the brow!
And, in parting from you now,
Thus much let me avow—
You are not wrong, who deem
That my days have been a dream;

title: Barter
author: Sara Teasdale
lines: Life has loveliness to sell,
All beautiful and splendid things,
Blue waves whitened on a cliff,
Soaring fire that sways and sings,

title: To Celia
author: Ben Jonson
lines: Drink to me only with thine eyes,
And I will pledge with mine;
Or leave a kiss but in the cup,
And I'll not look for wine.

title: Requiem
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
lines: Under the wide and starry sky,
Dig the grave and let me lie.
Glad did I live and gladly die,
And I laid me down with a will.
